title: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK
name: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK
goal: Leave the future version of you one exact phrase that points back into the task.
steps:
1. Before stopping, picture the exact next movement and current reasoning.
2. Hold one short phrase that tells you where to resume.
3. End the task without mentally reopening the whole plan.
4. On return, use the phrase and continue from that exact point.
numberedSteps:

win: The task ended with the next movement and reasoning preserved, so return did not require reopening the whole plan.

name: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD

goal: Sort claims about another person's mind into known, inferred, and unknowable.
steps:
1. Picture three boxes: KNOWN, INFERRED, UNKNOWABLE.

4. Leave the unknowable box empty of action.

title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
name: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
ritual_name: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
goal: Reduce exactly one kind of access without shutting down the entire relationship.
steps:
1. Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.

SET THE CONTACT DOSE
FRAME WIDENED
plain:
SET THE CONTACT DOSE

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Choose the smallest contact dose that preserves both connection and steadiness.

STEPS
1. Before contact, choose frequency, length, allowed topics, location, and an exit phrase.
2. Start with the lowest dose that keeps both connection and steadiness.
3. Review afterward using your body and behaviour, not guilt.

WIN
The amount of contact was chosen before the interaction and reviewed using body and behaviour afterward.

MIND BEND
Contact is a dose, not only yes or no. Changing the dose can reveal what level the relationship can actually handle.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Frequency → Start Lowest → Use Body

SAFETY
PAUSE
Reduce or end contact when boundaries are ignored or safety is compromised.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
name: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: See who carries the hidden work of the relationship over a set period.
steps:
1. Over a set period, note who starts contact, adjusts, repairs, plans, and follows up emotionally.
2. Allow for real differences in time, health, or capacity.
3. Discuss the pattern by category, not accusation, and ask for one clear rebalance.

title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
name: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
ritual_name: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
goal: Ask the question that could genuinely prove your assumption wrong.
steps:
1. Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
2. Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
3. Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.

title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
name: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
goal: Use a stable open posture without treating posture as a prediction about the outcome.
steps:
1. Take a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety.
2. Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
3. Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
ritual_name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: Prefer the option whose failure becomes visible while correction is still practical.
steps:
1. Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

TAKE UP 5% MORE SPACE · SAFETY CLOSER
plain:
TAKE UP 5% MORE SPACE

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Expand your posture slightly and notice which words become easier to access.

STEPS
1. Widen feet, elbows, chest, or seating position by a small manageable amount.
2. Keep the change below performance or dominance.
3. Observe what the expanded shape signals internally and which words become easier to access.

WIN
A small increase in physical space changed the internal signal without becoming dominance or performance.

MIND BEND
Posture can constrain language; taking a little more space may make options available that felt inaccessible in a collapsed shape.

FORMULA FLOW
Widen Feet → Keep Change → Observe Shape

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stay compact when wider posture would make the situation less safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL
name: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL
goal: Allow a small safe tremor to complete without clamping down or exaggerating it.
steps:
1. If medically safe and oriented, permit a small tremor rather than clamping it down.
2. Track its location, rhythm, and whether choice remains intact.
3. Let it stop, continue, or migrate without exaggeration.
4. Ground when the movement ends.

title: UNWIND IN REVERSE
name: UNWIND IN REVERSE
goal: Release a tension chain in the reverse order that it built.
steps:
1. Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.
numberedSteps:

numbered_steps:
1. Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.
win: Each muscle group handed the release onward until you could compare the original bracing point with its starting state.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Release a tension chain in the reverse order that it built.

STEPS
1. Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.

WIN
Each muscle group handed the release onward until you could compare the original bracing point with its starting state.

MIND BEND
Tension can accumulate as a sequence — reversing the order may give the body a more intelligible route out than relaxing everything at once.

FORMULA FLOW
Recall Muscle → Soften Work → Pause Handoff → Finish Original

SAFETY
PAUSE
Avoid manipulating painful, injured, or medically affected areas.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
name: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
goal: Complete one safe defensive movement slowly, then return all effort to zero.
steps:

4. Compare resting pressure, movement range, and urge before and after.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
name: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Use an imagined stable line as a reference without forcing your inner state to copy it.
steps:
1. Picture a stable horizontal line or horizon.
2. Notice its imagined stillness beside the movement inside your body and mind.
3. Do not force inner movement to match the line.
4. Let the stable image become a reference for one slow breath.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
name: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Use near, middle, and far sounds to reopen the sense of space around you.
steps:
1. Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.

goal: Keep only the room function that supports the next safe action and dismiss the rest for now.
steps:

name: COUNT EVERY OPEN LOOP

steps:

title: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
name: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
goal: Protect one active concern while giving the next item and the rest clear places to wait.
steps:
1. Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE.
2. Put only one concern in ACTIVE, one likely next item in WAITING, and mentally route everything else to ARCHIVE with a clear retrieval cue.
3. Give the active concern a protected time box.

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Protect one active concern while giving the next item and the rest clear places to wait.

STEPS
1. Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE.
2. Put only one concern in ACTIVE, one likely next item in WAITING, and mentally route everything else to ARCHIVE with a clear retrieval cue.
3. Give the active concern a protected time box.

WIN
One concern occupied ACTIVE, one sat in WAITING, and everything else had a retrieval cue in ARCHIVE.

MIND BEND
Working memory overload is partly a queueing problem. A thought can wait more quietly when it knows where its turn lives.

FORMULA FLOW
Create Positions → Wait Route → Give Active

SAFETY
PAUSE
Expand active capacity only when parallel monitoring is genuinely required.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

steps:

title: PARK WHAT YOU CAN’T KNOW YET
name: PARK WHAT YOU CAN’T KNOW YET
ritual_name: PARK WHAT YOU CAN’T KNOW YET
goal: Park a problem until the missing information needed to think usefully actually exists.
steps:
1. Name what is missing: another person’s decision, a test result, a future opening, or a resource.
2. Name what change would make thinking useful again.
3. Until that happens, store the problem with that trigger and stop working it.

title: ISSUE THE DECISION RECEIPT
name: ISSUE THE DECISION RECEIPT
goal: Give a completed decision a receipt so doubt has a specific rule for reopening it.
steps:
1. Picture the decision, main reason, date, one simple action, review date, and conditions that justify reopening.
2. Seal it in your mind.
3. When doubt returns, compare it with the reopening conditions instead of arguing the decision again from emotion.
numberedSteps:

title: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
name: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
ritual_name: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: Route a returning concern to one real destination or mark it undeliverable.
steps:
1. Assign the concern to one place: a named person, calendar slot, document, task name, or deliberate release.
2. Say the address in your mind and route the thought there each time it returns.
3. If no useful address exists, mark the thought UNDELIVERABLE and let it pass without rerouting.
numberedSteps:

3. Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Find a work-rest gear that matches actual strain instead of your prediction about strain.
steps:
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

GOAL
Find a work-rest gear that matches actual strain instead of your prediction about strain.

STEPS
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

WIN
A short work cycle with a deliberate ending revealed whether the next ratio should increase, hold, or finish.

MIND BEND
Anticipated effort and experienced effort are different measurements. Testing the gear replaces dread with data.

FORMULA FLOW
Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop for pain, illness, exhaustion, agitation, compulsive timing, or any task where interruptions create safety risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: Act where you have control, ask where you have influence, and release what you can only watch.
steps:

title: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
name: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
goal: Delay one answer-seeking urge and watch whether the need for information survives the wait.
steps:
1. When the question demands an answer, picture it and delay asking for a short, chosen interval.
2. Track urge intensity at beginning, middle, and end without researching.
3. Decide afterward whether information is still needed for action or only for relief.

goal: Plan from what is likely and supported, not from what is merely possible.
steps:
1. Say three lines: ‘It is possible that…’; ‘It is likely that…’; ‘The evidence supports…’.
2. Do not move an idea upward without a reason.
3. Plan from likelihood and safety needs, not possibility alone.

title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
name: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
goal: Prepare the useful first moves for two plausible outcomes without choosing a favourite too early.
steps:
1. Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit.
2. Prepare any step useful in both branches now.
3. Delay preference until evidence selects the path.

title: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
name: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
ritual_name: SWAP OUTCOME CONTROL FOR PROCESS CONTROL
goal: Score yourself on a process you control instead of an outcome you can only influence.
steps:
1. Name the desired outcome and cross it out as the score.
2. Substitute one visible process variable fully under your control—calls made, honest minutes practised, applications sent, boundary delivered.
3. Check success only on that variable for the chosen period.
numberedSteps:

title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
ritual_name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
goal: Collapse repeated clues that all came from the same source before judging how much evidence you have.
steps:
1. Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.
numberedSteps:
1. Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.
numbered_steps:

3. Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.
win: Echoes from one person, event, article, assumption, mood, or retelling became a single source family.
mindBend: Five clues can create false confidence when they are copies of one origin. Independence matters more than raw count.
mind_bend: Five clues can create false confidence when they are copies of one origin. Independence matters more than raw count.

Give extra thinking time only to topics that can name both a question and a useful result.

A thought without a clear question or deliverable lost its meeting time and attention returned to direct life.

Thinking feels productive by default. Requiring an agenda reveals how often the mind is holding meetings with no decision on the agenda.

plain:
MARK THE QUALITY DROP

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Stop when your thinking quality clearly drops and keep the last conclusion you could still trust.

STEPS
1. Pick your warning signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower understanding, repeated searches, or no new ideas.
2. When two signs appear, stop and keep the last reliable conclusion.
3. Rest before reopening the issue.

WIN
Two warning signs ended the thinking round before more searching could make it worse.

MIND BEND
Past a certain point, more thinking can make certainty stronger while accuracy gets weaker. Stopping can protect the best answer you already reached.

FORMULA FLOW
Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery

SAFETY
PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
name: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
ritual_name: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
goal: Name the guarantee you hope checking will give you, then ask whether information can really provide it.
steps:
1. Finish: ‘If I keep checking, I hope to guarantee that…’.
2. Ask whether any amount of information can truly provide that promise.
3. Gather only information that could change your action. Carry the remaining uncertainty without more checking.

title: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
ritual_name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Review only the turning point slowly enough to keep observation separate from motive.
steps:
1. Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Run those ten seconds once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep that one fact. End the review before building another explanation.

win: One visible change—pause, volume, face, movement, or reply length—was kept while the review ended before explanation multiplied.

title: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
name: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
goal: Let the best-supported thought guide the decision instead of giving every thought the same vote.
steps:
1. For each important thought, rate the evidence, source quality, freshness, and relevance.
2. Do not calculate a total; just rank them.
3. Let the strongest thought guide the action while weaker thoughts stay noted but do not decide.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
ritual_name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: Turn a repetitive thought loop into simple images and interrupt the first repeated meaning.
steps:
1. Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

title: DEMOTE THE HEADLINE EXPERIENCE
name: DEMOTE THE HEADLINE EXPERIENCE
goal: Give the dominant thought or sensation equal status with three background details.
steps:
1. Hold the dominant sensation or thought with three background what you notices—one sound, one contact point, one visual feature.
2. For a contained interval, give all four equal attentional weight without imagining a separate watcher.
3. Notice how centrality changes.

title: CATCH THE MOMENT ‘MINE’ ARRIVES
name: CATCH THE MOMENT ‘MINE’ ARRIVES
goal: Catch the extra moment when a thought or sensation changes from 'there' to 'mine'.
steps:

3. Do not try to change either moment.

steps:

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT

goal: Use real task feedback while letting self-commentary remain faint and unanswered at the edge.
steps:
1. Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

steps:

4. Include the sense of room around your body.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
name: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Remove one emotion temporarily to learn what it was contributing, then restore the whole stack.
steps:
1. Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
numberedSteps:
1. Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
numbered_steps:
1. Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.

title: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
name: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
goal: Notice the feeling of being ‘the watcher’ without having to keep that position in place.
steps:
1. Notice the subtle feeling that says ‘I am the observer’.

3. Let awareness continue without holding a separate watcher in place.
4. Return to an ordinary action straight afterward.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
name: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.
2. What do you fear will happen.
3. What would make one step acceptable.
4. Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
name: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
goal: Map the full trigger-to-result loop and change one link instead of fighting the whole system.
steps:
1. Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.

3. Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Try that small change once.

1. Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Try that small change once.

WIN
A single point in the sequence shifted once, creating fresh evidence about how the larger pattern responds.

MIND BEND
Complex habits can feel indivisible until one link changes; a loop only needs one altered connection to stop being exactly the same loop.

FORMULA FLOW
Imagine Parts → See Links → Find Lever → Test It

SAFETY
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look.
steps:
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

title: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
name: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
goal: Keep a sound decision closed unless new evidence meets your rule for reopening it.
steps:
1. Decide what new evidence would be strong enough to reconsider the choice.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
name: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
goal: Move one inherited rule across different settings and keep only what remains ethical and workable.
steps:
1. Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
name: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: Shrink a broad belief until it states where, when, and with whom it actually fits.
steps:
1. Say the belief silently.
2. Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Picture one real case where the belief does not fit.
5. Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Begin the required move before you feel ready and remove the strongest competing cue.

STEPS
1. Keep only the required move active.
2. Choose the one task that matters now.
3. Cover or mute the strongest distraction.
4. Name the exact next action you will return to.

WIN
One task stayed active, one distraction lost access, and the exact next action was saved for return.

MIND BEND
Readiness is often a prediction about comfort. Reducing competition can make action possible before that prediction changes.

FORMULA FLOW
Set Out → Pick One → Block Noise → Set Return

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Choose one issue, one next action, and one listening turn.

STEPS
1. Notice when several issues start entering the same conversation at once.
2. Slow your pace one notch.
3. Identify the next action you need.
4. Restate what you heard before replying.

WIN
Several concerns stopped entering at once, and the reply was restated before another issue was added.

MIND BEND
Stacked issues make even a solvable conversation feel global; one issue can create enough space for useful feedback.

FORMULA FLOW
Unmix Story → Lower Heat → Name Request → Leave Space

SAFETY
PAUSE

This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

plain:
THE LINE YOU CAN KEEP

PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Decline in one clear sentence and let guilt exist without giving it veto power.

STEPS
1. Name the request you want to decline.
2. Name the limit you actually need.
3. Notice the guilt without treating it as proof you are doing harm.
4. Speak no in one clear sentence without over-explaining.
5. Let the other person have their reaction without taking it back as your responsibility.

WIN
The limit was spoken without over-explaining, and the other person's reaction stayed on their side of responsibility.

MIND BEND
Guilt can be the feeling of breaking an old compliance rule, not evidence that the new boundary is harmful.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Request → Name Limit → Notice Guilt → Say No → Release Reaction

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

plain_text:
BOUNDARY HOLDS

PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Keep the stated boundary unchanged while the pressure to weaken it rises and falls.

STEPS
1. Notice the point pressure starts pushing you to weaken the boundary.
2. Keep the stated boundary unchanged.
3. Wait until your hands slow.
4. Focus on the decision you are keeping.

WIN
Your hands slowed, the original limit stayed intact, and the decision remained the one you had chosen.

A boundary can feel wrong simply because another person keeps pushing on it. Pressure tests stability, not necessarily fairness.

title: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
name: CUT THE AFTER-SOCIAL LOOP
goal: Stop looping over an awkward moment by separating what happened from the extra meaning your mind is adding.
steps:
1. Say the exact words or action you keep running through your mind once, with no commentary.
2. Name one fact about how the other person actually responded. If you do not know, say “I don’t know.”
3. Name the harsh conclusion your mind added afterward.
4. Replace it with the smallest fairer conclusion that still fits the facts.
5. Return to one ordinary action in the present.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Separate what can still be addressed from what is already over, then choose one proportionate next step.

STEPS
1. Name the one part of the event you are still carrying.
2. Separate what can still be addressed from what is already over.
3. Choose one reasonable next step, or deliberately choose to leave the event finished.

WIN
The carried part of the event became either a reasonable action or a deliberate decision to leave it finished.

MIND BEND
Resentment keeps the past active when it cannot tell whether there is still a job to do. Separating repairable from over creates an exit.

Use Detail → Ask Clearly → Close Loop

title: BRIDGE, NOT PROOF
name: BRIDGE, NOT PROOF
goal: Hear the person's full reply before seeking immediate proof that they understand your hurt.
steps:
1. Notice the urge to make the other person understand your hurt immediately.
2. Own your share without a speech.
3. Wait before acting on the first pressure.
4. Wait until the other person finishes.
5. Name the unresolved issue aloud.

title: MOTIVATION OR FRICTION?
name: MOTIVATION OR FRICTION?
goal: Find out whether disengagement is really low motivation or a fixable blocker before judging the person.
steps:
1. Name only what you can observe: late replies, low output, silence, missed steps—not “doesn’t care.”
2. List three possible blockers such as unclear work, overload, a skill gap, conflict, low value, or low energy.
3. Pick one question that could separate low motivation from a practical blocker.
4. Ask it neutrally, or prepare to ask: “What is making this hard to move?”
5. Set one small next step from what you learn.

title: ASK FOR THE RESOURCE
name: ASK FOR THE RESOURCE
goal: Ask directly for the resource needed to protect a specific work outcome.
steps:

2. State the resource you need in one sentence.

4. Offer one lower-cost or smaller fallback if useful.
5. Ask for a clear yes, no, or alternative.

title: LIMIT, THEN OPTION
name: LIMIT, THEN OPTION
goal: State the non-negotiable limit to an authority figure and offer an alternative only if it is real.
steps:

3. Voice no in one clear line without over-explaining.
4. Offer one workable alternative only if you genuinely can.
5. Stop after the boundary is clear.

PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Make one feedback action visible, do it first, and close the review after marking the change.

STEPS
1. Name the one feedback point you will act on.
2. Turn it into an observable result.
3. Put the first action where your attention can find it.
4. Complete that action before reviewing the rest.
5. Mark what moved, then close the exchange.

A single point became a concrete result and an actual first move before the rest was reconsidered.

plain:
BAD NEWS, NEXT MOVE

PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Deliver the bad fact plainly, then move straight to the decision you can still control.

STEPS
1. State one specific fact that another person could verify.
2. Separate the bad-news pressure from the decision you still control.
3. Name the one action you will take next.

WIN
One verifiable fact and one next action remained after the pressure of the news was separated from the response.

MIND BEND
Bad news removes some options but not all agency. The next controlled move keeps the message from becoming helplessness.

FORMULA FLOW
Use Detail → Pick Lane → Check Result

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Choose the leadership priority and stop polling once the next decision is yours to make.

STEPS
1. Notice the leadership tension.
2. Keep today's leadership priority in view.
3. Make the next decision without polling again.

WIN
Approval pressure stayed present without reopening the decision to another round of reassurance.

MIND BEND
Leadership can become popularity management when every decision is repeatedly sent back to the room for permission.

title: LIVING EDGE, CLEAN EXIT
name: LIVING EDGE, CLEAN EXIT
goal: Accept what already happened without turning acceptance into approval.
steps:
1. Name what happened without changing whether it was right or wrong.
2. Say, “Accepting that it happened is not approving it.”
3. Notice what energy is being spent fighting the fact that it already occurred.
4. Choose one boundary, repair, or next action that still belongs to you.
5. Let the event remain unacceptable if it was unacceptable, while releasing the demand that reality be different.

5. Do not reopen it unless new information appears.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Stop paying for a perfect ending when a clean enough ending already protects what matters.

STEPS
1. Name the last detail you keep polishing, checking, or waiting to feel settled about.
2. Ask what real harm would happen if you stopped now. Ignore discomfort that is not actual harm.
3. Set one ‘enough’ line: accurate enough, kind enough, complete enough, or safe enough.
4. Take one closing action—send, save, archive, leave, or stop.
5. Do not reopen it unless new information appears.

WIN
The ending became complete enough to close without demanding that every trace of discomfort disappear.

MIND BEND
Perfection can turn closure into an endless fee. An ending only needs to protect what matters, not erase every uneasy feeling.

FORMULA FLOW
Find Detail → Check Harm → Set Enough → Close → No Reopen

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do not use ‘good enough’ to skip safety, consent, legal, financial, or irreversible checks that truly matter.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALARM, NOT VERDICT
name: ALARM, NOT VERDICT
goal: Lower the panic load without testing your heart sensations or forcing your breathing.
steps:
1. Keep your eyes open and name three edges or corners you can see.
2. Slow one visible movement—your hands, feet, or walking pace—without forcing your breathing.
3. Tell a safe person, “I’m having a panic surge. Stay with me for a minute.”

win: Your attention widened to the room, one movement slowed, and a safe person was brought into the moment.
mindBend: Body alarm becomes louder when every sensation is treated as evidence needing inspection. External orientation interrupts that closed feedback loop.

mind_bend_text: Pressure creates a false sense that action must happen at the same speed as emotion. Delay proves those clocks are separate.
full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Put time and distance between rising pressure and any risky action.

STEPS
1. Notice the first sign that pressure is rising.
2. Do not act on the first surge.
3. Move your gaze to a neutral, steady surface.
4. Contact a live support person or service.

WIN
The first surge passed without action, attention moved to something neutral, and live support was contacted.

MIND BEND
Pressure creates a false sense that action must happen at the same speed as emotion. Delay proves those clocks are separate.

FORMULA FLOW
Notice Wave → Wait Lane → Change Place → Stay Connected

SAFETY
PAUSE
Move away from access, money, apps, substances, traffic, or other hazards. Contact a trusted person or qualified service if the urge feels difficult to manage safely. Call Triple Zero (000) for immediate danger.
This is brief self-help, not treatment or emergency care.

plain:
NAME THE GROUND

PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Use simple reality anchors and another person when body thoughts are amplifying each other.

STEPS
1. Check the current date aloud.
2. Name one cue for a steadier speaking pace without explaining.
3. Stay with the chosen support contact.

WIN
The date and speaking pace became external reference points while support stayed connected.

MIND BEND
Amplification thrives when sensation and interpretation keep confirming each other. A plain external fact introduces information from outside that loop.

FORMULA FLOW
See Edges → Cool Pace → Stay Support

SAFETY
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and orient to the room. Stop if symptoms intensify, you feel faint, or a medical problem may be possible. Call Triple Zero (000) for an emergency; otherwise use qualified medical advice. Do not induce or test symptoms.
This is brief self-help, not diagnosis or treatment.

title: BRING IN A REALITY PARTNER
name: BRING IN A REALITY PARTNER
playTime: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
play_time: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
goal: Do not test reality alone and bring in a trusted person and qualified support.
steps:
1. Stop testing the experience alone and avoid acting on unverified conclusions.
2. Contact a trusted person who can stay physically or verbally present.
3. Say, “I feel unsafe and need help checking what is real.”
4. Use the crisis or emergency options shown in the Safety box.
5. Stay connected until a qualified professional takes over.

goal: Leave immediate hazards and let another person help when your body is too highly charged for safe judgement.

2. Choose a quieter known place without driving yourself there.
3. Tell someone clearly that you cannot slow down safely.

5. Stay with support until a professional can assess you.

goal: Do not act on an unverified suspicion; stay with a reliable person while it is professionally assessed.
steps:
1. Do not confront, travel, spend, post, or retaliate on the suspicion.
2. Call someone known for being calm and reliable.
3. State what you noticed and what you fear without adding certainty.
4. Let that person contact urgent professional help with you.
5. Remain together until the concern is safely assessed.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
45–90 seconds

GOAL
Set an unsolvable question down and take a step that does not depend on its answer.

STEPS
1. Name the question in five words.
2. Say, ‘Not solvable in this round.’
3. Pick a step that does not need the answer.

WIN
The question was named, declared outside this round, and work continued without solving it.

MIND BEND
Some questions become powerful because every next action is made conditional on answering them. Removing that condition shrinks their control.

FORMULA FLOW
Make Cue → Set Aside → Check Loop

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

title: THE NEW-INFORMATION TEST
name: THE NEW-INFORMATION TEST
goal: Test whether more analysis is adding information before giving it another round.
steps:
1. Notice whether this round of analysis has produced any genuinely new information.
2. Separate what happened from the role you are assigning yourself.
3. Set any extra work aside.
4. Check the first action against one immediate fact.
5. Reduce the remaining question to three words.

title: LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN
name: LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN
goal: Stop fighting the thought and continue one small task without checking whether it left.
steps:
1. Say, “This thought is allowed to be here for this minute.”
2. Notice one sound or object outside your head without using it to escape or prove anything.
3. Start one small task while letting the thought remain in the background.
4. Do not check whether the thought has faded before continuing.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Put a chosen priority beside the thought and act on that priority without answering the mental command.

STEPS
1. Say, “My mind is giving me an instruction.”
2. Name one priority that exists outside the thought.
3. Choose one finishable action that serves that priority.
4. Do the first ten seconds.
5. Keep the thought unanswered and name where you will resume.

WIN
The first ten seconds of a priority-based action happened while the thought remained unresolved and non-authoritative.

MIND BEND
A thought can use command-shaped language without possessing command authority. Behaviour is where authority is actually granted.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Command → Name Priority → Choose Action → Start Ten → Leave Unanswered

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
